Shared architecture: The same substantial medieval Cenyri civic arena in Gwynthor: an OPEN-AIR oval sand fighting ground, pale warm limestone masonry, two tiers of stepped stone seating, dark oak pitched canopy roofs over the uppermost seating, two opposing arched fighter gates at sand level, and one modest covered honor gallery. Slate roofs, restrained red banners. This is a medieval Gaelic-inspired fantasy town, not a Roman Colosseum. No enormous imperial scale; no precise seat count implied.
Scene: Input image 1 is STYLE AND LOCAL MATERIAL reference only: the neighboring Gwynthor theater, do not copy its facade or theater ornaments. Input image 2 is the existing HOUSE DRAIG heraldry, use its red wyvern on an ivory ground very sparingly on a single hanging banner above the main gate, no new crest design. A distant three-quarter slightly elevated establishing view of the complete civic arena EXTERIOR, showing its broad curved outer wall, a large arched main public entrance, smaller side arches, and dark oak canopy roofs following the open ring. The near oval rim is low enough to glimpse the upper far seating across the open interior. A generous empty cobbled forecourt below, a few restrained Cenyri gabled town roofs beyond, clean blue sky with soft clouds. Clear afternoon sunlight. Arena should feel wide and substantial, not a narrow shop or closed theater building.
Constraints: Calm readable uncluttered composition, generous usable space, no people, no text, lettering, logo, watermark, modern stadium fittings, floodlights, plastic chairs, scoreboard, magical effects, blood or corpses. Opaque full-frame image, portrait 2:3. Keep the entire architecture coherent, with plausible perspective and clear doorways.
